description: Capabilities for the main window. Capability scope is intentionally NARROW at startup -- $APPDATA/** (per-dataset state, prefs, operations.log, originals/), $APPCACHE/** (ephemeral deface tmp under the bundle-id cache dir; mkdir-via-appCacheDir lives here, see src/lib/deface/tauriExecutor.ts), plus bundled $RESOURCE/** (importer manifests, validator schema, MNI templates, mindgrab weights) and nothing more. The renderer has no shell execute permission; import and deface process spawning is routed through Rust commands that select fixed executables and validate argv shapes. On dataset open the renderer invokes the `allow_dataset_scope` Rust command with a token previously minted by `pick_dataset_directory` / `pick_file`, which uses Tauri 2's runtime fs + asset-protocol scope APIs to widen access to the user-picked dataset root. Import flows additionally use the narrower `allow_fs_scope` for non-viewer source paths (DICOM / MEG sources, PET metadata) — fs scope only, no asset protocol — so a compromised renderer cannot stream those bytes through `asset://` even though it can read them. Pre-open XSS can only reach the three bundled locations; post-open, only the datasets the user actually selected in this session. Append-only at runtime by Tauri 2 design -- closing+reopening the app is the only way to drop a previously-opened scope. See ARCHITECTURE.md §6 for the policy and trade-offs. Write-class permissions are declared in string form (no per-permission `allow` arrays) so they fall back to `fs:scope` -- the runtime widening only reaches that global scope, and a per-permission `allow` array would shadow it (Tauri's permission system checks per-permission scope BEFORE the plugin's runtime scope). $RESOURCE/** stays in fs:scope but writes there are blocked at the OS layer (the .app bundle / Linux install prefix is read-only). The `deny` rules below exclude the Rust-managed trust file AND the cloud-share per-backend token files from renderer access — a compromised renderer cannot forge trust-set entries or peek at brainlife/openneuro JWTs even though both files live under $APPDATA.
